cases.xfail: period policy: the planner is not yet required to record a period that departs from the data's coverage as a decision, so a plan can narrow the period without saying so. Retire this marker when a departure is always a recorded decision.

turns.message: How did life expectancy in Kenya change from 1900 to 2023?

rubrics.property: The period the plan or the answer covers is the period the user asked for, 1900 to 2023, or the departure from it is stated: as a decision with a reason on the plan card, or in the closing message when no plan was proposed. A plan that silently uses another period, or an answer that presents a shorter period as the one asked for, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

cases.xfail: requested-output accounting: nothing yet requires each output the user asked for to be planned, declined with a code or put to the user, so one can drop out silently. Retire this marker when the plan maps every ask.

turns.message: Show Kenya's life expectancy as a line chart, give me the latest value as a stat card, and rank the East African countries by it.

rubrics.property: Each output the first message asked for (the line chart of Kenya's life expectancy, the latest value as a stat card, the ranking of the East African countries) is produced as a component, set out as a step on the plan card, declined in the closing message with its reason, or put to the user as a question. An output that is neither produced nor mentioned is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

cases.xfail: conversation digest: the previous closing message reaches the next turn cut at 280 characters, so an offer made at its end can be gone when the user says yes. Retire this marker when the previous closing message is carried whole.

turns.message: Show life expectancy in Kenya. End your answer by offering one specific follow-up, and wait for my reply.
yes

rubrics.property: The second turn carries out the follow-up the first turn's closing message offered, with its own data or components, and does not ask what 'yes' refers to. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

cases.xfail: source reuse: a source found with a blocking warning (role or time text dropped) can still be reused by the planner as if it answered the whole part. Retire this marker when a reused source must carry no blocking warning.

turns.message: How much aid did France give Kenya in the year before last, by sector?

rubrics.property: When a search result for a part of the question carried a warning that the search had not understood the part's place or period text, the closing message says which words were not read, and no figure from that part's source is presented as answering them. When no search result carried such a warning, answer yes.

cases.xfail: loop guard: an unchanged plan step that failed deterministically can be proposed and run again, whatever the brief says. Retire this marker when the repeat is refused before it runs.

turns.message: top 10 countries by health spending per person

rubrics.property: When a plan step fails with a refusal a retry cannot change, no later plan or fetch in the conversation puts the same step again: each differs from the failed one, or the closing message says what could not be done and why. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: France's aid to Africa

rubrics.property: The answer to 'France's aid to Africa' covers the African countries only, or the turn asks the user a question or declines with a reason. It never adds recipient rows that are regional, income-group or all-developing-country totals to country rows, and no yearly figure it gives exceeds France's whole ODA to all recipients, which is about $18bn a year in recent years. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: France's aid to Africa
How about as a share of France's total aid

rubrics.property: No share the second turn gives is above 100%. A share above 100% is allowed only when the message says why (for example, a gross figure over a net one) or when the turn declines or asks instead of giving the share. A share stated without such a reason is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Total aid from G7 to Africa since 1965
turns.elicitation_text: Add up the seven G7 countries' aid to Africa

rubrics.property: The turn ends with the total of the G7 countries' aid to Africa since 1965 drawn as a component, or with a question to the user that was answered and led to that total. A closing message that says the plan failed, could not be translated, or the calculation is unavailable, with no total, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Help me calculate net flows to Ghana combining aid and debt
turns.elicitation_text: Keep aid and debt flows as separate series; do not add them

rubrics.property: Before any figure that combines aid and debt flows is shown, the turn asks the user how to combine them, and the question or the closing message says that official development assistance loans appear in both the aid and the debt flows. Figures shown after the user's answer follow that answer. A combined figure shown before that question, or with no such question, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: How much aid does France provide per person
How about in grant equivalents since 2018?

rubrics.property: The grant-equivalent aid per person is France's whole grant-equivalent ODA from the DAC1 headline series divided by its population, or the turn asks which source to use. A figure built by summing recipient-level Creditor Reporting System rows, which leaves out core contributions to multilaterals and unallocated aid, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: How much aid does France provide per person
How about in grant equivalents since 2018?
What happened?

rubrics.property: The third turn's answer to 'What happened?' restates where the figure on screen comes from (the source dataset or series) and what it covers. An answer that only says the data cannot establish causes, with no source and scope, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Do you have any climate finance data

rubrics.property: The closing message states in one sentence what the series it offers covers and what it lacks (for example a worldwide total with no donor or recipient split), and gives the first and last values of that series. A message that presents a weak match as complete climate finance data is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

cases.xfail: climate markers: the CRS pipeline drops the policy markers, so the catalogue holds no OECD climate finance and only a worldwide total can be offered. Retire this marker when the markers are ingested.

turns.message: Do you have any climate finance data

rubrics.property: The answer offers OECD climate finance with donor and recipient detail (the Creditor Reporting System climate markers for mitigation and adaptation), not only a worldwide total. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: France's imputed multilateral ODA to Kenya, 2015 to 2024. France's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya for education, 2015 to 2024

rubrics.property: Both requested series are produced for 2015 to 2024: France's imputed multilateral ODA to Kenya and France's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya for education. They are shown as two series and are not added into one figure. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: How much do African countries spend on government health expenditure?

rubrics.property: The plan reads Africa as its member countries: the step that retrieves the data names 'each member of Africa' or lists African countries one by one, and the answer gives figures for individual African countries. A plan whose retrieval names Africa alone, as one region with one figure, is a no, as is an answer that gives only a single total for Africa. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Who are Kenya's top 5 creditors?

rubrics.property: The plan and answer use an outstanding external-debt stock for Kenya, not a debt-flow series, and rank the five largest creditors on the creditor or origin dimension. The answer names five creditors. A total for Kenya with no creditor ranking, a ranking of countries, or a net-flow measure is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Rank the top five African countries by outstanding external debt in the latest year.

rubrics.property: The plan and answer use an outstanding external-debt stock, retain Africa as its member-country scope, and rank five African countries. The plan may not replace Africa with a worldwide ranking, one total for Africa, or a creditor, recipient, donor or other flow-side breakdown. The answer names five African countries. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: What were gross ODA disbursements from the G7 in 2022?

rubrics.property: The answer states one 2022 figure for the G7 as a whole and says it is the total DAC publishes for the G7, not the G7 members' figures added up. An answer that lists the seven members' figures, or that says it added the members' figures together, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Bilateral plus imputed multilateral aid from France to Kenya, 2015 to 2022, summed

rubrics.property: The answer states that the bilateral part is net ODA (net disbursements) and gives the reason, that DAC counts a donor's total contribution to a recipient as net bilateral ODA plus imputed multilateral ODA. An answer that sums the two without naming the bilateral basis, or that names a gross bilateral basis, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: general government debt service by creditor for 2031
I said general government not PPG
That is incorrect

rubrics.property: The first turn's answer breaks general government debt service down by creditor, or states plainly that it declined that part and why. An answer that says the creditor breakdown is not available or not held in the data, when the plan ranked or kept creditors, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

After the user says 'general government not PPG', the reply names the series as general government debt service and does not treat the user's wording as a mistake. A reply that restates the series as public and publicly guaranteed debt without naming general government as the debtor type, or that tells the user that general government sits inside PPG as a correction, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

After 'That is incorrect', the reply either changes the answer for a stated reason drawn from the series on screen, or restates what the series is and asks what the user sees differently. A reply that repeats the earlier explanation of IDS debt categories without reference to the series on screen is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: DT.TDS.DEGG.CD by creditor for 2031

rubrics.property: The answer states the series as general government external debt service, with the creditor breakdown, from World Bank International Debt Statistics. An answer that treats the code as unknown, or asks the user to name the measure, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

The answer names DT.TDS.DEGG.CD as the World Bank code of the series it shows. An answer that does not name the code, or names it without tying it to the World Bank series shown, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show Kenya's life expectancy at birth.

rubrics.property: The closing message states Kenya's latest available life-expectancy value and that value's observed period. It does not add a first, historical, or extra endpoint because the user asked for neither a span nor a change; the dataset's coverage range does not count as a requested period. The returned component facts cover the requested Kenya series. A chart without the dated latest value in the closing message is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Compare life expectancy in Kenya and Uganda.

rubrics.property: The closing message gives both Kenya's and Uganda's requested or latest available life-expectancy values, with each value dated by its own observed period. The returned component facts cover both requested series. A response that gives only one country's value or period is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Rank Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, Zambia, Malawi, Mali, and Niger by life expectancy at birth in 2023, highest to lowest. Show a bar chart and give a brief conclusion.

rubrics.property: The returned component facts collectively cover Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, Zambia, Malawi, Mali, and Niger at 2023, and a completed rank step shows that their ordering was computed. The closing message gives a brief conclusion supported by only the figures needed for that conclusion and does not repeat the full twelve-country ranking. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

Every numerical difference, total, percentage, or count in the closing message is already stated in a completed step detail or component fact summary. A calculation inferred from chart values alone is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show life expectancy in Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania since 2000.

rubrics.property: The successful component shows all three requested series. The closing message gives a brief conclusion and does not list the first and last values for every series unless the user asked for those endpoints. It may compare only observed endpoints or relationships that a completed analysis result explicitly states. It must not call a series steady, lowest throughout, or the largest change, or describe any intermediate period, unless a tool result explicitly establishes that claim. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show life expectancy in Kenya as a line chart.
Replace that line chart with a table.

rubrics.property: The line-chart component id on the first turn is absent from the final canvas. The final canvas includes a table for the requested Kenya life-expectancy view; other companion cards may remain. The second turn completed both removal and chart-making, and its closing message confirms the replacement without a data recap. Adding a table without removing the original line chart is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show life expectancy at birth in Kenya and South Sudan from 2000 to the latest available year. Give each series' first and latest values in the reply.

rubrics.property: The closing message gives Kenya's first and latest values and South Sudan's first and latest values, each dated by its own observed period in the returned component facts. The component facts cover both series for the requested 2000-to-latest view. If the returned facts show different start periods, the reply preserves that difference. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Rank Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, Zambia, Malawi, Mali, and Niger by life expectancy at birth in 2023, highest to lowest. Show a bar chart, give a brief conclusion, and state Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, and Nigeria's values in the reply.

rubrics.property: The returned component facts collectively cover Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, Zambia, Malawi, Mali, and Niger at 2023. The closing message states Kenya's, Uganda's, Ghana's, and Nigeria's values, each with its own observed period. It does not repeat the full twelve-country ranking, though it may state other figures needed for its brief conclusion. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show life expectancy at birth in Kenya since 1980 as a line chart, and tell me what it was in 1990.
How has life expectancy at birth in Kenya changed?

rubrics.property: The closing message says whether Kenya's life expectancy rose or fell between the two periods it states, and says nothing about how it moved in the years between them. A message that gives the two values without saying which way the figure moved is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: France's aid to Africa
How about as a share of France's total aid

rubrics.property: The second turn's closing message gives the share as a percentage and says it is France's aid to Africa as a share of France's total aid. A percentage with no statement of what it is a share of is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

turns.message: Show aid to Malawi by donor as a bar chart. In the reply, give the value of the smallest donor on the chart and Iceland's value.

Show life expectancy at birth in 2023 for Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, Senegal, Zambia, Malawi, Mali, and Niger as a bar chart, and state the values for Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, Rwanda, and Zambia in the reply.
Show aid to Malawi by donor
Which donors give the most to Malawi?
Which donors give the most aid to Malawi?

rubrics.property: The closing message names the single year its ranking of donors to Malawi is for, and says how many donors have data for that year or that the ranking is among the donors with data for that year. The message may call them donors, providers or members; the count and the year are what is scored, whatever the noun. A message that ranks donors without naming the year, or that names only a span of years, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.

The closing message names a second year, different from the year its ranking is for, and states how many donors that second year covers: a newer year with the number of donors it has so far, or an earlier year with the larger number of donors it had. The message may call them donors, providers or members; the count and the year are what is scored, whatever the noun. A message that names no second year, names one without a count, or says only that newer data is incomplete without a count, is a no. This property always applies and is never inapplicable.
